article.headline: Unusual Whales Pipes Live Market Data Into AI Assistants via MCP
article.lede: Unusual Whales, a financial analytics company that built its reputation exposing congressional trading patterns, has released a server that lets AI assistants query live options and equity market data on demand. The product, launched in March 2026, uses Anthropic's open Model Context Protocol to turn any connected AI into an on-call analyst with access to the same institutional signals traders pay hundreds of dollars a month to monitor. It is the first official MCP server from a major financial data platform.
article.body:
The server exposes more than a hundred endpoints. *Options flow* — real-time options contract activity that functions as a leading indicator of institutional intent, since large options buyers often move before the underlying stock — sits alongside *dark pool prints* (block trades executed on private, institutional-only exchanges, reported after the fact with NBBO context), *sweeps* (intermarket orders that execute across multiple venues simultaneously, signaling maximum urgency), congressional trades, quarterly 13F filings, insider transactions, short interest, and technical indicators including RSI, MACD, and VWAP. A set of thirty pre-built prompts — “dark-pool-scanner,” “congress-tracker,” “morning-briefing” — provides analytical workflows without writing code.

The underlying infrastructure is the **Model Context Protocol** (MCP), an open standard Anthropic released in November 2024. Anthropic described it as “a USB-C port for AI applications” — a standardized handshake, built on JSON-RPC 2.0, that lets AI hosts such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, and VS Code connect to external tools without custom per-platform integration work. The protocol is not proprietary; Block (SQ), the payments and fintech conglomerate, was among the named early adopters at its launch.

Unusual Whales is bootstrapped — no outside funding — and was founded around 2020. It first attracted wider attention through financial transparency research: its 2021 report on congressional stock trading was cited by Bloomberg and Reuters and prompted six separate bills within a week of publication. The company has since built a subscription platform aggregating options flow, dark pool data, and regulatory filings, priced from free (delayed data) to roughly $100 a month for real-time premium access. Named data licensees include Public.com, the brokerage app, and Perplexity, the AI search engine.

The appeal of AI-mediated synthesis is real: options flow and dark pool prints are individually noisy, and their signal sharpens with cross-reference. *Golden sweeps* — Unusual Whales' term for sweep orders exceeding $1 million in premium — can move markets on their own; cross-referencing them against earnings calendars, insider filings, and congressional disclosures simultaneously was previously a task requiring multiple subscriptions and manual interpretation. The MCP server is MIT-licensed and distributed as an npm package; authentication requires a paid API key, with historical tape data carrying an additional $250-a-month charge.

A 2026 competitive review noted the platform's breadth is “unmatched” in its price tier while flagging a genuine limitation: it tells users what traded, not why mechanically. Deep options analytics — dealer gamma positioning by volatility regime, volatility surface calibration — remain outside its scope. That caveat aside, no major financial data platform had previously shipped an official MCP server, and the integration could compress the development cycle for AI-native trading tools from months to days.

concepts.definition: Real-time data on options contract activity, specifically large orders filled at or above the ask price — indicating a buyer willing to pay up. Calls skew bullish, puts bearish. Widely used as a leading indicator of institutional intent, since options buyers often telegraph moves in the underlying stock before those moves appear on the equity tape.

Block trades executed on private, institutional-only exchanges (dark pools) and reported to the public tape only after execution. Dark pools let large buyers conceal their moves from high-frequency algorithms and the public market. Providing NBBO context alongside a print reveals whether the institution paid a premium or discount to the prevailing public spread.

Intermarket sweep orders that execute across multiple exchanges simultaneously in rapid succession, prioritizing speed over price. The urgency is the signal — a buyer willing to fill across many venues at once is typically expressing high conviction. Unusual Whales tracks individual sweeps and flags aggregated sweep activity as particularly significant.

An open standard created by Anthropic in November 2024 for connecting AI applications to external data sources and tools. Built on JSON-RPC 2.0, it standardizes the handshake between an AI host (such as Claude or Cursor) and external servers, replacing bespoke per-platform integrations with a universal protocol. A data provider that builds one MCP server reaches every compatible AI client.

The best available bid and ask prices for a security, aggregated in real time across all U.S. exchanges and mandated by SEC Regulation NMS. Providing NBBO context alongside a dark pool print reveals whether an institutional trade occurred at a premium or discount to the public market.

Quarterly SEC disclosures required from institutional investment managers holding more than $100 million in qualifying equity assets. 13Fs reveal which funds hold which stocks, but are filed 45 days after quarter-end, making them a lagging indicator of institutional positioning.

Unusual Whales' proprietary term for options sweep orders exceeding $1 million in total premium. The company treats them as particularly significant short-term directional signals because the buyer is both urgently large and willing to pay up across multiple exchanges.

repos.summary: The official TypeScript MCP server package for Unusual Whales, published on npm as @unusualwhales/mcp. Exposes 100+ data endpoints across 14 categories — options flow, dark pool, congressional trades, institutional 13F filings, insider transactions, and more — alongside 30 pre-built analytical prompts. MIT-licensed and compatible with Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and Windsurf.

article.fact_check: The tweet frames the server as giving 'Claude' exclusive access, but the MCP server works with any MCP-compatible AI host — Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Perplexity, and others. The 'entire options and stock market' phrasing is marketing license: the server surfaces Unusual Whales' proprietary data platform, not a direct exchange feed. The data is comprehensive but filtered through Unusual Whales' ingestion and presentation layer.

poster_unusual-whales.blurb: Unusual Whales is a fintech data platform and X account focused on options flow analysis, dark pool activity, and congressional stock trading disclosures. The account aggregates and surfaces unusual or large-volume options trades that may signal informed positioning, alongside real-time tracking of trades filed by U.S. lawmakers under the STOCK Act. It gained mainstream visibility around 2021–2022 during the meme stock era and grew to over one million followers by surfacing politician trades in an accessible, often viral format. The account operates alongside a paid analytics platform at unusualwhales.com.
poster_unusual-whales.credibility_note: Unusual Whales does not editorialize on individual trades — it surfaces raw STOCK Act filings and options flow data, which limits direct bias, but presentation choices (which trades to highlight) can imply significance that isn't always there. The account is largely anonymous; no individual founder is prominently credited in public sources.
